expected.body: A 4-year-old girl presents with episodic watery diarrhea, a scaly photosensitive rash, and intermittent ataxia. Laboratory studies confirm impaired intestinal absorption of neutral amino acids including tryptophan. Diagnosis: Hartnup disease, in which tryptophan malabsorption depletes the precursor pool for niacin synthesis, producing pellagra. Key teaching: any condition limiting tryptophan availability can cause pellagra even without a niacin-deficient diet.
